title: Always Encrypted
description: Secure sensitive columns with Always Encrypted, ensuring data is never exposed to the SQL Server process in plaintext.

blocks.text: Always Encrypted ensures that sensitive data such as credit card numbers, government IDs, and health records remains encrypted inside the client application. The SQL Server process, including administrators, never sees plaintext values. Encryption and decryption happen in the client driver using keys stored outside the database, such as in the Windows Certificate Store, Azure Key Vault, or a hardware security module.

blocks.title: How It Works
blocks.text: The client driver intercepts queries, encrypts parameter values before sending them to SQL Server, and decrypts result sets after receiving them. SQL Server stores only ciphertext and performs operations on encrypted values.

Always Encrypted supports two encryption types. Deterministic encryption always produces the same ciphertext for the same plaintext, enabling equality joins, lookups, and grouping. Randomized encryption produces different ciphertext each time, providing stronger security but preventing equality operations and indexes.

cards.title: Deterministic
cards.description: Same plaintext always generates the same ciphertext.
pros: Can create indexes and primary keys

cards.title: Randomized
cards.description: Same plaintext generates different ciphertext each time.
cons: Cannot join or group on encrypted values

blocks.text: Always Encrypted uses two key types. The Column Master Key (CMK) is a key-protecting key stored outside SQL Server. The Column Encryption Key (CEK) is an encrypted symmetric key that actually encrypts the column data. The CEK is encrypted by the CMK and stored in the database as ciphertext.

terms.definition: An asymmetric key or certificate stored outside SQL Server, typically in the Windows Certificate Store or Azure Key Vault.
A symmetric key that encrypts column data. It is encrypted by the CMK and stored in the database.
A secure, trusted execution environment within the client driver that can perform computations on encrypted data without exposing plaintext to the host process.

blocks.title: Create Column Master Key and Column Encryption Key
blocks.content: Create the encryption keys using SSMS or T-SQL. The CMK path points to the external key store location.
blocks.code:
-- Create Column Master Key in database
CREATE COLUMN MASTER KEY AppCMK
WITH (
    KEY_STORE_PROVIDER_NAME = N'MSSQL_CERTIFICATE_STORE',
    KEY_PATH = N'CurrentUser/My/3F9B8A2C1D4E5F6A7B8C9D0E1F2A3B4C5D6E7F8'
);
GO

-- Create Column Encryption Key protected by the CMK
CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY AppCEK
WITH VALUES (
    COLUMN_MASTER_KEY = AppCMK,
    ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256',
    ENCRYPTED_VALUE = 0x0123456789ABCDEF...
);
GO

blocks.title: Driver Requirements
blocks.text: Always Encrypted requires a client driver that supports it, such as .NET Framework 4.6+, .NET Core, or the ODBC Driver 13+ for SQL Server. Applications using older drivers will receive errors when querying encrypted columns.

blocks.title: Create a Table with Encrypted Columns
blocks.content: Define encrypted columns using deterministic or randomized encryption.
blocks.code:
CREATE TABLE [dbo].[Patients] (
    PatientId INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    NationalId NVARCHAR(20) COLLATE Latin1_General_BIN2
        ENCRYPTED WITH (
            COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = AppCEK,
            ENCRYPTION_TYPE = DETERMINISTIC,
            ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256'
        ),
    Ssn CHAR(11)
        ENCRYPTED WITH (
            COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = AppCEK,
            ENCRYPTION_TYPE = RANDOMIZED,
            ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256'
        ),
    BirthDate DATE
);

data.caption: Always Encrypted data flow between application and SQL Server
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Client Application] --> B[SQL Client Driver]
    B --> C{Encrypted Column?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Encrypt Parameters Using CEK]
    C -->|No| E[Send Plaintext]
    D --> F[Send Encrypted Query to SQL Server]
    E --> F
    F --> G[SQL Server Process]
    G --> H[Store Ciphertext Only]
    H --> I[Data File on Disk]
    I --> J[Return Ciphertext Results]
    J --> B
    B --> K[Decrypt Using CEK]
    K --> L[Return Plaintext to Application]
    M[Column Master Key in External Store] --> B

blocks.text: Enclave computations extend Always Encrypted by performing computations inside a secure enclave. This allows richer operations such as pattern matching, range comparisons, and aggregations on encrypted data without exposing plaintext to the SQL Server process. Enclave technologies include Intel SGX, AMD SEV-SNP, and VBS on Windows.

blocks.title: Always Encrypted Limitations
items: LIKE patterns on encrypted columns require enclave computations
Bulk import operations may not work with encrypted columns
Full-text search does not work on encrypted columns
Columnstore indexes cannot include encrypted columns
Change data capture does not capture encrypted values

blocks.title: Rotate the Column Encryption Key
blocks.content: Rotate the CEK without downtime by creating a new key and re-encrypting data.
blocks.code:
-- Step 1: Create a new CEK
CREATE COLUMN ENCRYPTION KEY AppCEK_V2
WITH VALUES (
    COLUMN_MASTER_KEY = AppCMK,
    ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256',
    ENCRYPTED_VALUE = 0xNEWENCRYPTEDVALUE...
);
GO

-- Step 2: Alter table to use new CEK (requires application restart)
ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Patients]
ALTER COLUMN NationalId
    ENCRYPTED WITH (
        COLUMN_ENCRYPTION_KEY = AppCEK_V2,
        ENCRYPTION_TYPE = DETERMINISTIC,
        ALGORITHM = 'AEAD_AES_256_CBC_HMAC_SHA_256'
    );
GO

blocks.title: Key Rotation Strategy
blocks.text: Rotate CEKs annually or after any suspected key compromise. Use a rolling strategy: create a new CEK, update the application to use it, then drop the old CEK.

items.text: Generate the CMK and store it in an external key store
items.hint: Azure Key Vault or Windows Certificate Store

items.text: Create the CEK and protect it with the CMK
Enable Column Encryption Setting in the connection string
Test deterministic vs randomized encryption for each column
items.hint: Deterministic for lookups, randomized for maximum security

items.text: Document key rotation schedule and recovery procedures
items.hint: Without the CMK, encrypted data is unrecoverable

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always Encrypted keeps plaintext out of SQL Server by using client-side encryption.
Deterministic encryption supports equality operations; randomized does not.
The CMK stays outside SQL Server, and the CEK encrypts column data.
Enclave computations allow richer queries without exposing plaintext.
blocks.takeaway: Use Always Encrypted when you need strong guarantees that even DBAs cannot read sensitive data. Plan key rotation and recovery carefully.
